editorial:
You follow Stuart Long, a rough-around-the-edges boxer who heads to Los Angeles chasing money and fame after an injury ends his fighting days. While working at a supermarket, he meets Carmen, a Sunday school teacher who doesn't fall for his charm. To impress her, this lifelong agnostic starts showing up at church, and what begins as a crush slowly turns into something deeper. The movie has a warm, grounded feel, mixing humor with heavy life moments without getting too preachy.

Mark Wahlberg gives a committed, physical performance, and the supporting cast keeps the story moving. The pacing is steady, though some emotional beats feel rushed and the tone can swing between comedy and drama. If you enjoy true stories about second chances, faith, and personal change, this is a solid pick.
endingExplained: In the final stretch, Stuart survives the motorcycle crash but is diagnosed with a serious muscle disease. Instead of giving up, he enters seminary and becomes a Catholic priest. The ending shows him serving others despite his declining health, with his family and friends seeing how much he has changed. There is no big twist; the surprise is that his rough past becomes the reason he can connect with people. The movie closes on a hopeful note, showing his faith and humor staying strong even as his body weakens.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about second chances and faith.
